chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who has a right upon another man, so the debtor denies the right and swears that he owes nothing, and the creditor has no proof for his right. Is it permissible for us to revive his right by false testimony if there is fear of its loss? He said: That is not permissible due to the reason of fraud/deception.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use false testimony to collect a debt when the debtor denies it and there is no proof?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that using false testimony to recover a disputed debt is impermissible due to 'al-tadlis' (subtle deception), distinguishing it from simple lying. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the integrity of the evidentiary process, where the method of establishing truth must not itself be fraudulent, even if the underlying claim is valid. The ruling underscores the principle that justice requires not only a true claim but also a truthful means of proving it.
